name: Chapter 13: Oscillations
description: Periodic and oscillatory motion, SHM, phase, reference circle, velocity and acceleration, force law, energy, spring systems, simple pendulum

cards.term: Periodic vs oscillatory motion?
cards.definition:
Periodic: repeats at regular intervals
Oscillatory: periodic to-and-fro motion about a mean (equilibrium) position

cards.term: Is every periodic motion oscillatory?
cards.definition: No: every oscillation is periodic, but uniform circular motion is periodic without being oscillatory

cards.term: Oscillation vs vibration?
cards.definition:
No real difference.
Low frequency is usually called oscillation (tree branch)
High frequency is called vibration (guitar string)

cards.term: Why do real oscillations die out? How can they be kept going?
cards.definition: Damping (friction, dissipation); an external periodic force can keep them going (forced oscillations)

cards.term: How are waves related to oscillations?
cards.definition: A medium is a collection of coupled oscillators; their collective oscillations are waves

cards.term: Define period and frequency. Unit of frequency?
cards.definition: Period T: smallest interval after which motion repeats. Frequency ν = 1/T, in hertz (1 Hz = 1 s⁻¹)

cards.term: Example 13.1: heart beats 75 times a minute. Frequency and period?
cards.definition: 1.25 Hz, 0.8 s

cards.term: What does "displacement" mean in oscillations?
cards.definition: Change with time of any physical quantity: position, angle of a pendulum, capacitor voltage, air pressure in sound…

cards.term: Fourier’s theorem?
cards.definition: Any periodic function can be written as a superposition of sines and cosines of different periods

cards.term: Show that A sin ωt + B cos ωt is simple harmonic.
cards.definition: It equals \( D\sin(\omega t + \phi) \) with \( D = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2},\ \tan\phi = B/A \)

cards.term: Is it SHM, periodic, or neither?
cards.definition: sin ωt + cos ωt: SHM, T = 2π/ω; sin ωt + cos 2ωt + sin 4ωt: periodic, not SHM; T = 2π/ω; 3 cos(π/4 − 2ωt): SHM, T = π/ω; cos ωt + cos 3ωt + cos 5ωt: periodic, not SHM; T = 2π/ω; e^(−ωt), log ωt, 1 + ωt + ω²t²: non-periodic

cards.term: Example 13.3: is sin²ωt simple harmonic?
cards.definition: sin²ωt = ½ − ½ cos 2ωt: harmonic with period π/ω, but about the mean value ½, not 0

cards.term: Exercise 13.4(b): is sin³ωt simple harmonic?
cards.definition: No: sin³ωt = (3 sin ωt − sin 3ωt)/4, periodic (T = 2π/ω) but not SHM

cards.term: Define simple harmonic motion.
cards.definition: Motion in which displacement is a sinusoidal function of time:\[x(t) = A\cos(\omega t + \phi)\]

cards.term: Meaning of symbols in x = A cos(ωt + φ)
cards.definition: A: amplitude (maximum displacement); ω: angular frequency (rad/s); ωt + φ: phase (time-dependent); φ: phase constant (phase at t = 0)

cards.term: Identify: where is the particle and how fast at t = 0, T/4, T/2, 3T/4?
cards.definition: At +A (rest), 0 (vₘₐₓ, moving to −A), −A (rest), 0 (vₘₐₓ, moving to +A)

cards.term: Relation between ω, T and ν?
cards.definition: \[\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = 2\pi\nu\]

cards.term: What does the phase tell you?
cards.definition: The state of motion (position and velocity) at time t

cards.term: How many initial conditions fix a given SHM (known ω)?
cards.definition: Two: e.g. initial position and velocity, or amplitude and phase

cards.term: Does the period of SHM depend on amplitude?
cards.definition: No: T is independent of amplitude, energy and phase (unlike planetary orbits)

cards.term: Exercise 13.7: x(0) = 1 cm, v(0) = ω cm/s, ω = π s⁻¹. Amplitude and phase for x = A cos(ωt + φ)?
cards.definition: A = √2 cm, φ = −π/4 (= 7π/4). With sine: B = √2 cm, α = π/4

cards.term: SHM as the projection of uniform circular motion
cards.definition: The projection of uniform circular motion on a diameter is SHM: x = A cos(ωt + φ); fastest at centre, at rest at ±A

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
SHM · reference circle

A point moves uniformly round a circle. How does its shadow on a diameter move?

Imagine light from above.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
SHM · reference circle

A point moves uniformly round a circle. How does its shadow on a diameter move?

The shadow executes SHM: x = A cos(ωt + φ), with A = radius and ω = angular speed of the point.

It is fastest at the centre (v = ωA) and momentarily at rest at ±A.

cards.term: How is SHM related to uniform circular motion?
cards.definition: The projection of uniform circular motion on any diameter is SHM (reference circle, reference particle)

cards.term: A ball whirled in a horizontal circle, seen edge-on: what motion do you see?
cards.definition: To-and-fro SHM along a line

cards.term: Projections on the x- and y-axes: how do they differ?
cards.definition: Same amplitude and ω, but differ in phase by π/2 (cos vs sin)

cards.term: Is the restoring force in SHM the same as the centripetal force of the reference circle?
cards.definition: No: they are very different forces; only the projected motion matches

cards.term: Example 13.4(a): radius A, T = 4 s, starts at 45°, anticlockwise. x(t)?
cards.definition: \[x = A\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}t + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]

cards.term: Example 13.4(b): radius B, T = 30 s, starts at 90°, clockwise. x(t)?
cards.definition: \[x = B\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{15}t\right) = B\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{15}t - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]

cards.term: Exercise 13.11 (Fig. 13.20): x-projections of the two motions shown?
cards.definition: (a) x = −3 sin πt cm (b) x = −2 cos (πt/2) cm

cards.term: Velocity in SHM?
cards.definition: \( v = -\omega A\sin(\omega t + \phi) \); in terms of x: \( v = \pm\omega\sqrt{A^2 - x^2} \)

cards.term: Acceleration in SHM?
cards.definition: \[a = -\omega^2 A\cos(\omega t + \phi) = -\omega^2 x\]always towards the mean position

cards.term: Maximum speed and maximum acceleration?
cards.definition: \( v_{max} = \omega A \) at x = 0; \( a_{max} = \omega^2 A \) at x = ±A

cards.term: Phase relations between x, v and a?
cards.definition: v leads x by π/2; a is π out of phase with x

cards.term: Mnemonic: where is each quantity zero or maximum?
cards.definition: "Middle: fast, no force ends: still, big force": at x = 0, v max and a = 0 at x = ±A, v = 0 and |a| max

cards.term: Example 13.5: x = 5 cos(2πt + π/4) m. Displacement, speed and acceleration at t = 1.5 s?
cards.definition: x = −3.535 m; speed ≈ 22 m/s; a ≈ +140 m/s²

cards.term: Signs of v and a in SHM (Exercise 13.5)
cards.definition: At end A: v = 0, a +; At end B: v = 0, a −; Mid-point, going to A: v −, a = 0; 2 cm from B, going to A: v −, a −; 3 cm from A, going to B: v +, a +

cards.term: Exercise 13.6: which is SHM: a = 0.7x, a = −200x², a = −10x, a = 100x³?
cards.definition: a = −10x only (a ∝ −x)

cards.term: Force law for SHM?
cards.definition: \( F = -kx \) with \( k = m\omega^2 \): restoring force ∝ displacement, towards the mean position

cards.term: Period of a mass on a spring?
cards.definition: \( T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac mk} \), \( \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac km} \)

cards.term: Linear vs non-linear oscillator?
cards.definition: Linear: F ∝ −x exactly. Non-linear: extra x², x³ terms (real systems at large amplitude)

cards.term: Example 13.6: mass between two identical springs k. Period?
cards.definition: Net force −2kx →\[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2k}}\]

cards.term: Effective spring constant
cards.definition: Two springs in parallel (or on both sides of a mass): k₁ + k₂; Two springs in series: k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂); Spring cut into two equal halves: each half 2k

cards.term: Exercise 13.13: spring k with mass m at one end (a) vs masses m at both ends (b), each pulled by F. Extension and period?
cards.definition: Extension F/k in both. T = \( 2\pi\sqrt{m/k} \) for (a), \( 2\pi\sqrt{m/2k} \) for (b) (each half acts as a 2k spring)

cards.term: Exercise 13.8: spring balance, 0–50 kg over 20 cm; a hanging body oscillates with T = 0.6 s. Its weight?
cards.definition: k = 50 × 9.8/0.2 = 2450 N/m → m ≈ 22.3 kg → weight ≈ 219 N

cards.term: Exercise 13.9: 3 kg on a spring k = 1200 N/m pulled 2.0 cm. Frequency, max acceleration, max speed?
cards.definition: ω = 20 rad/s → ν ≈ 3.2 Hz; aₘₐₓ = 8.0 m/s²; vₘₐₓ = 0.4 m/s

cards.term: Exercise 13.10: same spring; x(t) if timing starts at the mean position, at maximum stretch, at maximum compression?
cards.definition: x = 2 sin 20t, 2 cos 20t, −2 cos 20t (cm): only the initial phase differs

cards.term: Exercise 13.17: why does a floating cork pushed down execute SHM?
cards.definition: The extra buoyancy is ∝ depth pushed (Aρₗgx): a restoring force ∝ −x;\[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{h\rho}{\rho_l g}}\]

cards.term: Teacher addition: period of a liquid column (total length L) oscillating in a U-tube (Exercise 13.18)?
cards.definition: \[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{2g}}\]restoring force from the level difference 2x

cards.term: Exercise 13.14: locomotive piston, stroke 1.0 m, ω = 200 rad/min. Maximum speed?
cards.definition: vₘₐₓ = ωA = 200 × 0.5 = 100 m/min

cards.term: Kinetic and potential energy in SHM?
cards.definition: \[K = \tfrac12 kA^2\sin^2(\omega t + \phi),\quad U = \tfrac12 kx^2 = \tfrac12 kA^2\cos^2(\omega t + \phi)\]

cards.term: Total energy in SHM?
cards.definition: \[E = \tfrac12 kA^2 = \tfrac12 m\omega^2A^2\]constant, ∝ amplitude²

cards.term: Period of K and U compared with the period of motion?
cards.definition: T/2: each peaks twice per oscillation

cards.term: Where is energy all kinetic, all potential?
cards.definition: All kinetic at x = 0; all potential at x = ±A

cards.term: At what displacement are K and U equal?
cards.definition: \[x = \pm\dfrac{A}{\sqrt2}\]

cards.term: Example 13.7: 1 kg on a 50 N/m spring pulled 10 cm. K, U and E at x = 5 cm?
cards.definition: K ≈ 0.19 J, U = 0.0625 J, E = 0.25 J (= ½ × 50 × 0.1²)

cards.term: Who noticed the periodic swing of a chandelier, timing it with his pulse?
cards.definition: Galileo

cards.term: Which force gives the restoring torque on a pendulum bob?
cards.definition: The tangential component mg sin θ; T − mg cos θ provides the centripetal force

cards.term: Why is a pendulum SHM only for small angles?
cards.definition: Restoring torque ∝ sin θ, and sin θ ≈ θ (radians) only for small θ — within ~1 % up to about 20°

cards.term: Period of a simple pendulum?
cards.definition: \[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac Lg}\]independent of mass and (small) amplitude

cards.term: Example 13.8: length of a seconds pendulum (T = 2 s)?
cards.definition: L = gT²/4π² ≈ 1 m

cards.term: Exercise 13.15: a pendulum has T = 3.5 s on Earth. On the Moon (g = 1.7 m/s²)?
Exercise 13.16: pendulum in a car going round a circle (radius R, speed v). Period?
cards.definition: \[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{\sqrt{g^2 + v^4/R^2}}}\](effective g includes v²/R)

cards.term: Teacher addition: pendulum in a lift accelerating up at a?
cards.definition: \[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g + a}}\](down: g − a; free fall: no oscillation)

cards.term: Exercise 13.1: which are periodic — swimmer’s return trip, displaced bar magnet, rotating H₂ molecule, arrow from a bow?
cards.definition: Bar magnet and rotating H₂ molecule; the swimmer and arrow do not repeat

cards.term: Exercise 13.2: which are (nearly) SHM — Earth’s rotation, mercury in a U-tube, ball in a bowl, polyatomic molecule vibrations?
cards.definition: SHM: U-tube mercury, ball in a bowl. Periodic but not SHM: Earth’s rotation, polyatomic vibrations

cards.term: Exercise 13.3 (Fig. 13.18): which x–t plots are periodic?
cards.definition: (b) and (d), each with period 2 s; (a), (c) are not (repeating one position is not enough)

cards.term: Correction: NCERT labels the Exercise 13.3 figure "Fig. 18.18", cites "Eq. (14.4)" and potential energy "in Chapter 6". Right references?
cards.definition: Fig. 13.18, Eq. (13.4), and Chapter 5 (Work, Energy and Power) — leftovers of the old numbering

cards.term: Chapter 13 formula sheet
cards.definition: Displacement: x = A cos(ωt + φ); Velocity: v = ±ω√(A² − x²); Acceleration: a = −ω²x; Spring: T = 2π√(m/k); Pendulum: T = 2π√(L/g); Energy: E = ½kA²

advancedHtml.backHtml:
Summary

Formula?

Displacementx = A cos(ωt + φ)
Velocityv = ±ω√(A² − x²)
Accelerationa = −ω²x
SpringT = 2π√(m/k)
PendulumT = 2π√(L/g)
EnergyE = ½kA²

cards.term: Chapter 13 concept checks
cards.definition: Every periodic motion is SHM: False (only F = −kx); A sum of two SHMs is always periodic: False (frequencies must be commensurate); Damped oscillation is strictly SHM: False; Period of SHM is independent of amplitude: True
